question.worked_solution:
To solve this equation, we need both exponential terms to have a common base. To do this, we rewrite the equation using $9={3}^{2}$ and $27={3}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
{({3}^{2})}^{y}={({3}^{3})}^{y-3}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule of exponents. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2y}={3}^{3(y-3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(3)$, we equate the exponents and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2y & =3(y-3) \\ 2y & =3y-9 \\ y & =9\end{aligned}
$$
